transcript: You know what makes me crazy? I'm sorry, can I say sorry? Can I say this? You know what makes me crazy? You know what makes me nuts? People who fundamentally misunderstand the last five years. Because Jason Robert Brown did not write the last five years in an effort to make himself look good and his ex wife look bad. Like, that's just not true. And all you need to do is look at their post marriage songs to know this. Because you look at Kathy's and it's all painting Kathy as a victim. It is all like, look at what you're doing to me. Those are Kathy's post marriage songs. Jamie's post marriage songs are g. Golly, it sure is hard not to cheat. And if I didn't believe in you. Where he's just like verbally berating her and then nobody needs to know where he is physically cheating on her. Even when you look at their last songs in the relationship, like, Kathy's is still hurting. She's like saying about how she's still hurting. And then Jamie's is uh, I could never rescue you. Like, it is very much him saying that he sees Kathy as the one who is at fault. And to that extent I understand where this misconception comes from, cause people are like, oh, well, Jamie is a Jason Robert Brown self insert. And to Jamie does not see himself as at fault. So therefore Jason Robert Brown must also not see himself As at fault. But at the same time, this show was written as a way for Jason Robert Brown to process his own divorce with the benefit of hindsight and I think also process a lot of internalized guilt that he felt for actions that he took during the course of his marriage. I don't think the point of the show is to determine who is the villain or who is in the right and who is in the wrong. Like, if you had to choose a villain, it's very clearly Jamie. And I think that Jason Robert Brown knows this. In fact, I know that he knows this cause someone once tweeted him, who do you see as the villain of the last five years? And he responded with a GIF of Alphabet going, it's me, it's me. So like, he knows.
